parts.text: In this experiment, you will measure the spring constant k of a spring by two different methods. The spring constant k of a spring is a measure of how difficult the spring is to stretch. Method 1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) • Attach the spring to the clamp, as shown in Fig. 1.1. • Suspend a mass m = 500 g from the spring. Fig. 1.1 • Pull the mass down a small distance (2–3 cm) from its rest position and release it. The mass oscillates up and down. The period T of the oscillations is the time taken for one oscillation. One complete oscillation of the mass is shown in Fig. 1.2. Fig. 1.2

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Measure the time t taken for 20 oscillations. Do not remove the mass from the spring. Record t in Table 1.1. [1] Table 1.1 m / g t / s T / s 500

ms.label: 1(a)(i)
ms.text: t recorded and in the range 16.5 to 19.5 (s)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the period T of the oscillations. Record your answer in Table 1.1. [1]

ms.label: 1(a)(ii)
ms.text: T calculation correct from candidate’s values

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate a value k 1 for the spring constant of the spring. Use the equation shown. Give your answer to an appropriate number of significant figures. k 1 = 19.7 T 2 k 1 = ................................................. N / m [1] Method 2

ms.label: 1(a)(iv)
ms.text: k1 calculation correct and 2 or 3 significant figures

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) With the 500 g mass still suspended from the spring, measure the stretched length l of the spring in centimetres to the nearest 0.1 cm. Do not include the loops at the ends of the spring in your measurement. Record l in Table 1.2. Table 1.2 m / g l / cm 500 400 300 200 100 [1]

ms.label: 1(b)(i)
ms.text: l recorded to the nearest millimetre

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Carefully remove the 100 g masses from the mass hanger, one at a time, and repeat the procedure in (b)(i) for m = 400 g, 300 g, 200 g and 100 g. Record each value of l in Table 1.2. [1]

ms.label: 1(b)(ii)
ms.text: all values of l present and decreasing

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Plot a graph of l / cm ( y -axis) against m / g ( x -axis). Start your axes at the origin (0, 0). Draw the best-fit line. m / g l / cm 0 0 [3]

parts.text: (iv) Determine the gradient G of your line. Show all working and indicate on the graph the values you use. G = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: v
parts.text: (v) An estimated value k 2 for the spring constant of the spring can be calculated using the equation k 2 = 1 G . Calculate k 2 using your value of G from (b)(iv) and the equation shown. k 2 = ................................................. N / m [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Two quantities can be considered to be equal within the limits of experimental accuracy if their values are within 10% of each other. Compare your values of k 1 from (a)(iv) and k 2 from (b)(v) . State whether your results indicate that the values can be considered to be equal.
